coverage.notes: SEL: NYSED benchmarks (3 goals, K-12 plus adult indicators), recommended for VOLUNTARY use. Portrait of a Graduate: adopted by the Board of Regents July 2025; NYSED memo (7/31/2025) says it does not change current graduation requirements and that required instructional alignment begins with the 2029 cohort (grade 9 in 2029-30). Reviewer: re-check both pages for later changes.

frameworks.name: New York State Social Emotional Learning Benchmarks (Equity Revisions)
frameworks.notes: Original benchmarks 2018; equity revisions 2022. Three goals: (1) self-awareness that nurtures identity and agency, (2) social awareness and interpersonal skills for supportive relationships, (3) intentional decision-making. Items here are the 10 base indicators (1A-3C); each has grade-band indicators (K-2, 3-5, 6-8, 9-10, 11-12) in the source. Titles are short paraphrases. Text was read from the Children's Institute-hosted copy of NYSED's document (nysed.gov's own PDF refused the download); confirm against NYSED's PDF before verifying. CASEL tags follow the document's own footnote (goal 1 = self-awareness and self-management, goal 2 = social awareness and relationship skills, goal 3 = responsible decision-making); the split within goals is a judgment call for the reviewer.

items.title: Understand emotions and how they relate to actions
items.summary: Identify one's emotions, see how they connect to what one does, and use that understanding to guide actions.

items.title: Explore personal and group identity
items.summary: Reflect on personal and group identity, including cultural background, and find outside supports for identity development.

items.title: Set and work toward goals; learn from mistakes
items.summary: Set personal and academic goals, take risks, own mistakes, and use them to grow.

items.title: Build empathy for others' feelings and perspectives
items.summary: Recognize and understand that other people feel and react differently based on their experiences and cultures.

items.title: Affirm identities, similarities and differences
items.summary: Recognize and affirm individual and group identities and differences, and engage respectfully in difficult conversations.

items.title: Communicate and interact across lines of difference
items.summary: Use a range of communication and social skills with individuals and groups, with empathy in every interaction.

items.title: Prevent, manage and resolve conflicts
items.summary: Prevent, manage or resolve conflicts, including those involving injustice, and express agreement or disagreement respectfully.

items.title: Consider safety, well-being and context in decisions
items.summary: Weigh individual and collective social, emotional and physical safety and the social context when making decisions.

items.title: Apply decision-making skills to shape outcomes
items.summary: Use decision-making skills to influence outcomes and strengthen agency in social and academic life.

items.title: Act to support school and community well-being
items.summary: Take action for the well-being of school and community, including standing against bias and injustice.

frameworks.name: New York State Portrait of a Graduate
frameworks.issuingBody: New York State Board of Regents / NYSED
frameworks.notes: Six interconnected attributes grounded in Culturally Responsive-Sustaining Education. Read from NYSED's one-page Portrait PDF (nysed.gov/sites/default/files/programs/grad-measures/portrait-of-a-graduate.pdf). Summaries are paraphrases.

items.title: Academically Prepared
items.summary: Strong foundation in the NYS learning standards, ready for college, careers, civic engagement, service and life.

items.title: Creative Innovator
items.summary: Uses imagination, curiosity and flexible thinking to solve problems and develop new ideas while adapting to change.

items.title: Critical Thinker
items.summary: Analyzes information, weighs evidence and finds connections across subjects to address complex issues.

items.title: Effective Communicator
items.summary: Expresses ideas clearly through speaking, writing and media, and listens to different perspectives.

items.title: Global Citizen
items.summary: Acts responsibly and ethically in local, global and digital communities and contributes to a diverse, democratic society.

items.title: Reflective and Future Focused
items.summary: Reflects on strengths and growth areas, sets goals, keeps supportive relationships and makes responsible decisions that protect well-being.

alignments.framework: New York State Social Emotional Learning Benchmarks (Equity Revisions)
alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Stay in Control of Your Spirit" (middle school, series: Conflict & Self-Government). FNE's stated objective: "Learners will identify signs that emotions are beginning to take control, practice a simple pause-and-reset process, and choose one respectful action that keeps their response aligned with their values." The lesson has students recognise when emotions start driving behaviour and choose a response, which is the same skill.

alignments.framework: New York State Social Emotional Learning Benchmarks (Equity Revisions)
alignments.rationale: Tune Your Brain game "Feelings Detective" (tagged self-awareness). FNE's catalog description: "Notice real cues in a scene, then pick every feeling that plausibly fits." Covers naming what someone feels from real cues; it does not by itself connect those feelings to the player's own actions.

alignments.framework: New York State Social Emotional Learning Benchmarks (Equity Revisions)

FNE's published description: "Understanding and naming emotions, managing reactions, building empathy, and developing the self-awareness that underlies every other social-emotional skill." The theme names understanding emotions and self-awareness. Program-level: shows the theme is part of the offering, not which lesson teaches it.

alignments.framework: New York State Social Emotional Learning Benchmarks (Equity Revisions)
alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Learn From Mistakes" (middle school, series: Responsibility & Ownership). FNE's stated objective: "Students will understand that mistakes are part of learning and growth. They will learn that a mistake is not their identity; it is information that can show them what needs attention, what needs practice, and what better choice can be made next time." The lesson frames a mistake as information about what to practise next and treats owning it as part of growth, the same skill.

They will learn that personal growth happens when they choose effort, practice, better responses, and steady learning, even when it feels ..." Covers choosing effort and steady learning for oneself.

Students choose a skill to strengthen, track it and adjust with feedback, which is goal-setting and monitoring. Limit: Goals are personal habits; it does not cover career or post-graduation planning.
